Subject: HelixAI - initial capacity ask for dedicated deployment

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the chat this morning — Helix is excited to move from pilot to a committed Dedicated slab for our customer-facing summarization API. Attached is a small sample of 7 days of traffic (helix_usage_sample.csv) and a short PDF with our SLO ask (90% of requests < 250ms, 99% < 600ms for responses up to 512 tokens, and we expect 2.5x daily peak vs median).

We'd like a quick estimate of tokens/sec headroom required to meet those SLOs for the model family we discussed (gpt-small-like ~7B, quantized). Also want recommendations for burst/quiet-hour policy and any fallback model suggestions if we hit saturation. Can you folks map this to an initial slab recommendation (GPU counts / instance types) and an operational fallback?

Appreciate a short note laying out options and any clarifying questions.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Head of Platform, HelixAI

Quick clarifying Qs before we run numbers:

If you can reply with those, we will produce a short note with two slab options: conservative (1.5x expected peak headroom) and compact (minimal acceptable headroom with aggressive caching/batching).

All — I parsed helix_usage_sample.csv and sketched a quick model. Summary below (high-level; assumptions noted):

Assumptions:
- Model profile: 7B transformer, int8 quantized inference path, typical token gen cost ~0.6ms/token on A100-40GB equivalent serving kernel (continuous-batching and KV cache present).
- Average response length: 180 tokens, 95th percentile length: 420 tokens (from sample).
- Peak multiplier: you confirmed 2.5x is on aggregate tokens/sec (Sanjay — please correct if concurrent metric).
- Streaming: 20% streaming, 80% non-streaming. Cold-start window acceptable up to 150ms for first token.

Modeling outputs (rounded):
- Median tokens/sec observed: 9,200 t/s (from CSV). Peak expected: 23,000 t/s (2.5x).
- Effective token processing time (including overheads): 0.8ms/token (kernel + RPC + queueing headroom) => 1,250 tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU core.
- Baseline GPUs needed to serve peak with 1.0x headroom (no spare): 18 GPUs (23,000 / 1,250 ≈ 18.4).

Headroom scenarios:
1) Compact (minimal): 1.25x peak headroom => target capacity = 29,000 t/s => ~24 GPUs. Expected p95 latency for 512-token requests: ~420ms (tight for 250ms SLO). Not recommended unless you accept SLO compromises and aggressive caching.
2) Conservative (1.5x): target capacity = 34,500 t/s => ~28 GPUs. Expected p95 ~280ms (closer to 250ms SLO; multi-pronged: warm KV cache + slight request shaping).
3) Premium (2.0x): target capacity = 46,000 t/s => ~37 GPUs. Expected p95 ~210ms (comfortable margin for 250ms SLO with streaming).

Burst policy suggestions:
- Configure burst buckets by route with token tokens/sec crediting (e.g., allow 3x for 2 minutes then fall back using token-leaky-bucket).
- Quiet-hours scaling: autoscale down to median capacity (≈ 9,200 t/s equivalent) with warmup prefetch to re-populate KV caches 10–15 minutes before expected traffic ramps.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
- Primary: gpt-small-7b-int8 (above). Fallback: 3B quantized variant (0.4ms/token kernel) — use for best-effort traffic when queue depth exceeds configured threshold; expected quality delta small for summarization.
- Secondary: enable partial-response streaming for large outputs to prioritize first-token p50.

Next actions:
- Sanjay: confirm peak multiplier interpretation (aggregate tokens/sec) and streaming percent.
- Ben & Ops: rough instance SKU recommendation (A100x or H100x) and sizing for GPU memory headroom.
- I'll produce a short table mapping tokens/sec ↔ GPU count per slab and expected p95 latency under our latency model.

Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer — Inference Capacity Modeling

Hi Sanjay — thanks, and appreciate the quick back-and-forth. Short customer-facing proposal below we can use in the deal doc and the HubSpot record.

Proposal (executive summary):
- Recommended slab: Dedicated pool of 28 A100-equivalent GPUs (conservative plan). Rationale: meets 1.5x peak headroom target, balances cost with latency SLO risk.
- Fallback policy: automatic route to 3B-quantized variant after queue depth > 200ms projected wait or when 95th-percentile token latency budget breaches. Implement partial-response streaming for large outputs to protect first-token latency.
- Autoscale & burst: allow 3x burst credit for up to 90s, with leaky-bucket backpressure and per-route token limits. Quiet-hours: scale to 9 GPUs (median-sized) with proactive KV warmups 10 minutes before predicted ramp.
- Expected SLO fit: with this slab and configured caching + batching we expect p95 for <=512 token responses to be ~250–300ms. If Helix requires strict 250ms p95 with 99.9% uptime, upgrade to Premium slab (37 GPUs) or accept additional engineering (model distillation / more aggressive quantization + network peering).

Operational items / asks:
1) Please confirm the peak multiplier (aggregate tokens/sec).
2) Sign-off on fallback model acceptance (Helix product team approval) — we can prepare A/B eval prompts.
3) Procurement: if you want the conservative plan, I'll attach a committed-slabs starter quote and dedicated SLA addendum.

I'll upload a short mapping table to the HubSpot deal and the shared Drive; links included above. Happy to walk through these numbers live if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
